\section[abonar]{abonar — to pay; to credit}

\label{lesson:ES-C632-abonar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the demand, then the Spanish for to be worth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: abonar}
\textbf{abonar} — \textquotedblleft{}to pay; to credit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Puede abonar la cantidad con tarjeta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You can pay the amount by card.}
\end{quote}

Formal, on bills and notices. It also means to fertilise.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{abonar} is built on \emph{bueno}, inherited from Latin \emph{bonus} 'good' (EtymDB): it first meant to make good, then to pay.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abonar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abonar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{abonar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the demand, then the Spanish for to be worth, then say \emph{abonar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does abonar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pay; to credit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la mensualidad]{la mensualidad — the monthly payment}

\label{lesson:ES-C632-mensualidad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to be worth, then the Spanish for to pay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la mensualidad}
\textbf{la mensualidad} — \textquotedblleft{}the monthly payment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pago una mensualidad de cincuenta euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I pay fifty euros a month.}
\end{quote}

One monthly payment out of several.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mensualidad} is built on \emph{mensual}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{mensualis}, from \emph{mensis} 'month' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la mensualidad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la mensualidad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la mensualidad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to be worth, then the Spanish for to pay, then say \emph{la mensualidad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la mensualidad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The monthly payment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[fraccionar]{fraccionar — to split into instalments, to divide}

\label{lesson:ES-C632-fraccionar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to pay, then the Spanish for the monthly payment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fraccionar}
\textbf{fraccionar} — \textquotedblleft{}to split into instalments, to divide\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Puedes fraccionar el pago en tres meses.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You can split the payment over three months.}
\end{quote}

Common in shops and banks.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fraccionar} is built on \emph{fracción}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{fractio} 'a breaking' (EtymDB), from \emph{frangere} 'to break'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fraccionar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fraccionar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fraccionar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to pay, then the Spanish for the monthly payment, then say \emph{fraccionar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[ingresar]{ingresar — to pay in, to deposit; to be admitted}

\label{lesson:ES-C632-ingresar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the monthly payment, then the Spanish for to split into instalments.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ingresar}
\textbf{ingresar} — \textquotedblleft{}to pay in, to deposit; to be admitted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ingresé el dinero en mi cuenta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I paid the money into my account.}
\end{quote}

In Spain \emph{ingresar dinero} is to pay it in; much of Latin America says \emph{depositar}. \emph{Ingresar en el hospital} — to be admitted.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ingresar} is built on \emph{ingreso}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ingressus} 'an entering', from \emph{ingredi} and \emph{gradi} 'to step' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ingresar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ingresar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ingresar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the monthly payment, then the Spanish for to split into instalments, then say \emph{ingresar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does ingresar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pay in, to deposit; to be admitted\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la pensión]{la pensión — the pension; the guesthouse}

\label{lesson:ES-C632-pension}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to split into instalments, then the Spanish for to pay in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la pensión}
\textbf{la pensión} — \textquotedblleft{}the pension; the guesthouse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi abuela cobra una pensión.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandmother gets a pension.}
\end{quote}

Also a cheap guesthouse: \emph{una pensión en el centro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pensión} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{pensio} 'a payment', built on \emph{pendere} 'to weigh out, to pay' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la pensión}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to split into instalments, then the Spanish for to pay in, then say \emph{la pensión} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
